title: "No errors anywhere" is itself a clue, not a dead end
explanation: `cat /etc/cron.d/rotate-metrics` shows the job line has no output redirection at all — nothing after the command. Cron's default behavior for output like this is to try to mail it to the job's owner; `which sendmail` and `which mail` both coming back empty means there's no mail transport agent installed to deliver that mail. Whatever the job prints — including any error — is generated and then discarded, with genuinely nowhere for it to land.

title: You can't diagnose output you never captured
explanation: "The job never runs" and "the job runs and fails instantly" produce the identical outward symptom — an empty `/var/lib/metrics/archive/` — when there's no visibility into what actually happened. Before investigating further, add a redirection to the cron.d line itself so any future output has somewhere real to go: `*/5 * * * * trainee /opt/scripts/rotate-metrics.sh >> /var/log/rotate-metrics.log 2>&1`.

title: Now the real failure is visible
explanation: Running the script the way it'll now be captured (`/opt/scripts/rotate-metrics.sh >> /var/log/rotate-metrics.log 2>&1; cat /var/log/rotate-metrics.log`) surfaces `cp: cannot stat '/var/lib/metrics/metrics.log': No such file or directory` — a completely ordinary, easy-to-fix error that was invisible for as long as nothing captured it.

title: Trace the error to what's actually on disk
explanation: `ls /var/lib/metrics/` shows the real file is named `metrics.current.log`, not `metrics.log` — the script's `SRC` variable is hardcoded against a filename from before some earlier rename. `sed -i` on that one line points it at the file that genuinely exists.

title: Verify the archive appears, and keep the visibility fix
explanation: Re-running the job now produces a file under `/var/lib/metrics/archive/`. Keeping the `>> ... 2>&1` redirection in the cron.d entry matters just as much as fixing the path — without it, the next failure (a full disk, a permissions change, anything) disappears just as silently as this one did. Always give a cron job an explicit destination for its output before trying to diagnose why it "isn't working," or you're debugging blind.
